chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: The people say that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted twenty-nine days more often than he fasted thirty days.
So he said: They have lied. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast except complete months.
And that is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: “and that you complete the number.”
Thus, the month of Ramaḍān is thirty days, Shawwāl is twenty-nine days, and Dhū al-Qaʿdah is thirty days and never decreases; because Allah, the Exalted, says:
“And We appointed for Mūsā thirty nights.”
And Dhū al-Ḥijjah is twenty-nine days. Then the months are upon that pattern: one full month and one deficient month, and Shaʿbān is never completed.

key_terms.الْعِدَّةَ: the prescribed number or count to be completed
key_terms.تَمَامًا: complete in full, referring here to a full count of fasting days
key_terms.تِسْعَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ: twenty-nine, indicating a deficient lunar month
key_terms.ذُو الْحِجَّةِ: the twelfth month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.ذُو الْقَعْدَةِ: the eleventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, the month of obligatory fasting
key_terms.شَوَّالٌ: the month following Ramaḍān in the lunar calendar

ai.seo_question: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fast Ramaḍān as twenty-nine days or thirty days according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a ruling about the lengths of certain lunar months, especially Ramaḍān, and rejects the claim that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم more often fasted twenty-nine days. It supports the statement by citing Qur’anic wording about completing the count and mentions a recurring pattern among the months.
